# FEAT-011: Agent Integration (pi-agent-core)

> **Status**: [ ] Not started
> **Owner**: agent team
> **Depends on**: FEAT-001 (Monorepo Scaffold & CI), FEAT-002 (Yantra Protocol v0 — tool defs + semantic validator), FEAT-006 (Security Envelope — sanitizer chokepoint + AuditLogWriter)
> **Unblocks**: FEAT-007 (`ask` Pipeline) LLM synthesis path; FEAT-012 (CLI Polish) end-to-end audit story

---

## 1. Feature Goal

Deliver `packages/agent` — the **single, compiler-enforced chokepoint** for every LLM call in Yantra. Wraps `pi-agent-core` behind a thin internal `LLMClient` interface so the project is structurally decoupled from any one provider SDK, and so the sanitizer-first invariant is enforced at the type system, not aspirationally.

This feature lights up three load-bearing capabilities:

1. **Provider abstraction.** A `LLMClient` factory selects between `AnthropicLLMClient`, `OllamaLLMClient`, and `NullLLMClient` based on `LLM_PROVIDER` (env or config). Two real providers from day one (per memory.md), with `none` as a first-class mode — not a degraded fallback.
2. **Tool definitions are auto-generated from FEAT-002's Zod schemas — and FEAT-002 emits a vendor-neutral `ToolCatalog`.** No hand-maintained tool-call schema lives in this package; the agent consumes the emitted `TOOL_CATALOG` artifact and converts it once at startup to pi-agent-core's `AgentTool` shape via `pi-adapter.ts` — **this is the only place in the monorepo that knows pi-agent-core's tool-definition shape.** Touching a Step verb's signature in `packages/protocol` regenerates the catalog with zero edits here.
3. **Plan generation + validation + bounded re-prompt.** `generatePlan` sanitizes the prompt (the `Sanitized<T>` branded type makes raw strings a compile error), assembles a deterministic system prompt (generated tool catalog + hand-written guidance + schema version), calls `pi-agent-core`, schema-validates the response, semantic-validates it via FEAT-002's validator, and on failure builds a structured re-prompt context (offending JSON pointer + error) and retries up to `N` (default 2). Every call is wrapped by an audit higher-order that writes to `agent.jsonl` via FEAT-006's `AuditLogWriter` — no LLM call escapes the wrapper.

**`LLM_PROVIDER=none` returns a typed `LLMUnavailable` error.** Per memory.md §Error Handling: not a silent degradation. Callers (FEAT-007 `ask`, FEAT-012 CLI) pattern-match and either fall through to a deterministic alternative (rule-based summarizer) or render an actionable error message. The "spine works without LLM" contract from the plan is enforced at the type system: `NullLLMClient.generatePlan` returns `Result<never, LLMUnavailable>` so consumers cannot accidentally treat absence of an LLM as success.

**Why this package owns the boundary**: it is the **only** place in the monorepo allowed to `import 'pi-agent-core'`. The import-restriction lint rule (set up in FEAT-001) and a CI static-analysis grep enforce this — and per memory.md the rule is non-negotiable. Anything else that wants LLM output goes through `LLMClient`.

**Non-goals (deferred)**:
- LLM reanchor of locator chains (Phase 2 — protocol leaves the slot in `LocatorChain`).
- Discovery's bounded ReAct (Phase 3+ — out of MVP entirely).
- OpenAI provider (Phase 2 — adapter shape stays open).
- Cost-budget enforcement across runs (Phase 2 — per-call latency/cost are logged; aggregate budgeting is the executor's concern in FEAT-005).
- Streaming token-by-token output to the CLI (`pi-agent-core` supports it via `message_update`; MVP records but does not render token deltas — FEAT-012 prints the final response).

---

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

This package adds **no persistent storage of its own**. Its on-disk projection is `runs/<id>/agent.jsonl`, which is written by FEAT-006's `AuditLogWriter` — every agent invocation in this feature is responsible for paying through to that writer. All other state is in-memory and per-run.

### 2.1 On-Disk Artifacts

| Artifact | Owner / Writer | Shape | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `~/.local/share/yantra/runs/<run-id>/agent.jsonl` | `AuditLogWriter.appendAgentCall` (from FEAT-006) — invoked by **every** `LLMClient` call via the audit wrapper (TASK-010) | `AgentJsonlEntry` (see §2.2) | Append-only JSONL; flushed per append (per FEAT-006 contract); secrets never appear; prompt is always the *sanitized* form. |
| `packages/protocol/generated/tool-catalog.ts` | **FEAT-002** emits at build time | Vendor-neutral `ToolCatalog` (`ToolDefinition[]`) per `Step` discriminated-union variant | Consumed by `packages/agent` at runtime — no Zod runtime dep crosses the boundary; no pi-agent-core import either (protocol stays vendor-neutral per FEAT-002 TASK-009). The pi-agent-core translation happens here in `pi-adapter.ts`. Drift between protocol and agent fails CI (FEAT-002 guard). |
| `packages/agent/src/prompts/guidance.md` | Hand-authored in this feature; checked in | Markdown | Style + principles section of the system prompt. Versioned with the code. Changes are reviewed like code. |
| `e2e/golden/<intent>.golden.json` | Hand-authored fixtures; regenerated per LLM model bump | `{ intent, model, plan }` | Plumbing only in this feature (TASK-013); populated during MVP dogfooding. CI compares emitted Plan to golden on every dependency bump; intentional changes require explicit re-pinning. |

### 2.2 In-Memory Entities

All types live under `packages/agent/src/client/` and `packages/agent/src/plan/` and are re-exported from `src/index.ts`.

#### 2.2.1 `Sanitized<T>` — branded type (`src/sanitizer-guard.ts`)

The compile-time half of the sanitizer-first guarantee. A nominal brand on `string` (and recursively on objects containing strings) that **can only be produced by FEAT-006's `sanitize()`**. The `LLMClient` method signatures accept `Sanitized<string>` exclusively; passing a raw string is a TypeScript error.

```ts
declare const SanitizedBrand: unique symbol;
export type Sanitized<T> = T & { readonly [SanitizedBrand]: true };

/**
 * Type-cast helper. ONLY callable from packages/core/src/sanitizer/* (enforced by
 * ESLint import-pattern rule + CI grep). Any call site outside the sanitizer fails
 * the build. This makes Sanitized<T> structurally producible only via sanitize().
 */
export function brandSanitized<T>(value: T): Sanitized<T>;

/**
 * Runtime defense in depth — throws SanitizerGuardError if a value reaches the
 * LLMClient that wasn't produced by sanitize(). Implementation uses a WeakSet
 * populated by sanitize() (for objects) plus a per-process Map<string, true>
 * (for primitive strings — bounded to last N=10_000 entries with LRU eviction).
 */
export function assertSanitized(value: unknown): asserts value is Sanitized<unknown>;
```

The `assertSanitized` runtime check is a **belt-and-suspenders defense**. Type-erasure means `Sanitized<string>` is structurally indistinguishable from `string` at runtime; the WeakSet/LRU registry closes that gap. Memory.md §Security guarantee #2 is satisfied by (a) the type brand, (b) the runtime assertion, and (c) the CI grep on `LLMClient` call sites. Belt + suspenders + audit log.

#### 2.2.2 `LLMClient` — strategy interface (`src/client/interface.ts`)

The interface every consumer codes against. Three concrete strategies (`AnthropicLLMClient`, `OllamaLLMClient`, `NullLLMClient`) implement it.

```ts
import type { Plan, ValidationError, UsageCall, ToolCatalog } from "@yantra/protocol";
import type { ZodSchema } from "zod";

export interface LLMBudget {
  readonly maxCalls: number;            // hard cap on calls inside a single generatePlan invocation (re-prompts count)
  readonly maxLatencyMs: number;        // per-call timeout
  readonly maxTokensIn: number | null;  // null = provider default
  readonly maxTokensOut: number | null;
}

export interface GeneratePlanOpts {
  readonly sanitizedPrompt: Sanitized<string>;
  readonly toolCatalog: ToolCatalog;    // vendor-neutral, from FEAT-002 TASK-009; pi-agent-core translation lives in pi-adapter.ts
  readonly schema: ZodSchema;           // typically the Plan schema from protocol; allows test overrides
  readonly budget: LLMBudget;
  readonly workflowContext?: {
    readonly workflowSecrets?: ReadonlyArray<string>;
    readonly workflowLocators?: ReadonlyArray<string>;
  };
  readonly runId: string;               // for audit logging
  readonly taskId: string;              // for audit logging
}

export interface SummarizeOpts {
  readonly sanitizedInput: Sanitized<string>;
  readonly sanitizedPrompt: Sanitized<string>;
  readonly budget: LLMBudget;
  readonly runId: string;
  readonly taskId: string;
  readonly stepId?: string;             // populated when called from an llm_summarize step; null for ask-pipeline
}

/** Plan §7 / FEAT-002 §2.1.8: callers receive both the result AND the per-call usage record. */
export interface GeneratePlanResult {
  readonly plan: Plan;
  readonly usage: UsageCall;            // aggregated across re-prompts: totals over all attempts of this generatePlan call
}

export interface SummarizeResult {
  readonly text: string;
  readonly usage: UsageCall;
}

export interface LLMClient {
  /**
   * Generate a Plan from a sanitized user intent.
   * Runs schema + semantic validation; on failure rebuilds re-prompt context and retries up to budget.maxCalls.
   * Returns the validated Plan AND a UsageCall record aggregated across all attempts of this generatePlan call.
   */
  generatePlan(opts: GeneratePlanOpts): Promise<Result<GeneratePlanResult, LLMError>>;

  /**
   * Free-form LLM summarization over already-sanitized input (used by ask's LLM synthesis path and
   * by FEAT-005's llm_summarize step handler). No tool calls; plain text in, plain text out.
   * Still wrapped by the audit logger AND the UsageWriter (FEAT-005).
   */
  summarize(opts: SummarizeOpts): Promise<Result<SummarizeResult, LLMError>>;

  /**
   * Identity for logging and provider-drift tests. e.g., "anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-...",
   * "ollama:llama3.1:8b", or "null".
   */
  readonly providerId: string;
}

// Result<T,E> is a small, project-local discriminated union exported from packages/protocol or a shared utils package.
```

#### 2.2.3 `LLMError` — discriminated union (`src/client/interface.ts`)

```ts
export type LLMError =
  | { readonly kind: "llm_unavailable"; readonly reason: "provider_none" | "missing_api_key" | "ollama_unreachable"; readonly hint: string }
  | { readonly kind: "llm_timeout"; readonly elapsedMs: number; readonly budgetMs: number }
  | { readonly kind: "llm_provider_error"; readonly providerCode: string | null; readonly message: string; readonly retryable: boolean }
  | { readonly kind: "llm_validation_failed";
      readonly attempts: number;
      readonly errors: ReadonlyArray<ValidationError>;
      // Plan §7: user-facing one-line hint derived from the dominant failure class.
      // The CLI renders this directly; the structured `errors` go to report.md.
      readonly userFacingHint: string }
  | { readonly kind: "llm_budget_exhausted"; readonly callsMade: number; readonly maxCalls: number };
```

Each variant is a closed shape — consumers must pattern-match exhaustively. Custom error classes (`LLMUnavailableError`, `LLMTimeoutError`, etc.) extending `Error` are derived from these for `throw`-style call sites that want to bubble; the canonical surface is the discriminated union returned in `Result<T, LLMError>`.

**`userFacingHint` derivation** (per plan §7) — when `generatePlan` exhausts re-prompts, the orchestrator classifies the most common `ValidationError.code` across the collected attempts and maps it to a hint:

| Dominant error code | `userFacingHint` |
|---|---|
| `UnknownLocator` | "the AI referenced a UI element the workflow doesn't define — try naming the target more concretely" |
| `OutOfScopeVerb` | "the AI tried to perform a mutating action inside a `read-only-data` section — try splitting the task into read and write phases" |
| `MissingParam` | "the AI needs a value you didn't provide — re-run with `--params <key>=<value>` for the missing field" |
| `MissingSecret` | "the AI needs a credential not yet stored — run `yantra config set secret.<name>` first" |
| `MalformedPlan` (catch-all) | "the AI couldn't structure a valid plan — try rephrasing your request more concretely with specific URLs or named elements" |

The mapping table lives in `src/plan/user-facing-hints.ts` and is tested for coverage (every `ValidationError.code` from FEAT-002 has a hint).

#### 2.2.4 `AgentJsonlEntry` — audit log shape (consumed from FEAT-006; defined here)

```ts
export interface AgentJsonlEntry {
  readonly direction: "request" | "response";
  readonly run_id: string;
  readonly task_id: string;
  readonly provider_id: string;          // LLMClient.providerId
  readonly model: string;                // e.g., "claude-sonnet-4-20250514"
  readonly prompt_sanitized: string;     // the Sanitized<string> unwrapped at the audit boundary
  readonly system_prompt_hash: string;   // SHA-256 of the assembled system prompt (cheap dedupe/audit)
  readonly response: unknown;            // raw provider response (no secrets — sanitizer guarantees)
  readonly tool_calls: ReadonlyArray<{ tool: string; input: unknown }>;
  readonly latency_ms: number;
  // Token telemetry sourced from pi-agent-core (plan §6 / FEAT-002 §2.1.8 / FEAT-005 UsageWriter):
  readonly input_tokens: number;
  readonly output_tokens: number;
  readonly cost_estimate_usd: number | null;   // null for Ollama (local); positive for paid providers
  readonly step_id: string | null;       // populated for llm_summarize calls; null for plan-generation
  readonly attempt: number;              // 1 for first call; >1 for re-prompts
  readonly outcome: "ok" | "validation_failed" | "timeout" | "provider_error";
  readonly ts: string;                   // ISO-8601 UTC
}
```

Mandated by memory.md §Logging audit-events list. Two entries per call (`request`/`response`) so a partial failure is recoverable from the log.

**Each `response` entry that completes successfully (`outcome: 'ok'` or `'validation_failed'`) ALSO writes a `UsageCall` to the run's `usage.json` via the `UsageWriter` interface (owned by FEAT-005)**. The two writes happen in the same audit wrapper (TASK-010) so they cannot drift — if the agent.jsonl entry is written, the usage.json row is written too. `cost_estimate_usd: null` for Ollama (no provider pricing).

#### 2.2.5 `ProviderConfig` — config shape (`src/client/factory.ts`)

```ts
export type ProviderName = "anthropic" | "ollama" | "openai" | "none";

export interface ProviderConfig {
  readonly provider: ProviderName;
  readonly anthropic?: {
    readonly apiKey: { kind: "env"; name: "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" } | { kind: "keychain"; service: "yantra"; account: "anthropic.api_key" };
    readonly model: string;              // e.g., "claude-sonnet-4-20250514"
  };
  readonly ollama?: {
    readonly baseUrl: string;            // default "http://localhost:11434"
    readonly model: string;              // e.g., "llama3.1:8b" — see TASK-004 for recommended list
  };
  readonly openai?: { readonly apiKey: unknown; readonly model: string };  // Phase 2 — scaffold only
  readonly defaultBudget: LLMBudget;
}
```

Resolution order: `LLM_PROVIDER` env var > `~/.config/yantra/config.yaml` `provider:` key > default `"none"`. The factory **never** silently picks a provider — if `provider: anthropic` is configured but no API key is present, the factory logs a clear `pino.warn` and returns `NullLLMClient` so `LLMUnavailable` propagates downstream rather than failing mid-call.

#### 2.2.6 `SystemPromptAssembly` — deterministic prompt builder output (`src/prompts/assemble.ts`)

```ts
export interface SystemPromptAssembly {
  readonly text: string;                 // the full system prompt fed to pi-agent-core
  readonly schemaVersion: "0.1";         // mirrors protocol's SCHEMA_VERSION
  readonly toolCatalogHash: string;      // SHA-256 of the rendered tool catalog section
  readonly guidanceHash: string;         // SHA-256 of guidance.md content at assembly time
  readonly fullHash: string;             // SHA-256 of `text` — equality is the determinism contract
}

export interface AssembleOpts {
  readonly toolCatalog: ToolCatalog;
  readonly schemaVersion: "0.1";
  readonly guidanceMarkdown: string;     // injected; defaults to file contents at build time
}
```

`assemble(opts)` is a **pure function** — same inputs always produce the same `fullHash`. Property-tested. The hash is logged to `agent.jsonl` so audit consumers can detect prompt drift across runs.

#### 2.2.7 `RePromptContext` — re-prompt assembly state (`src/plan/generate.ts`)

```ts
export interface RePromptContext {
  readonly originalPrompt: Sanitized<string>;
  readonly previousRawResponse: unknown;
  readonly validationErrors: ReadonlyArray<ValidationError>;   // includes JSON-pointer paths
  readonly attempt: number;              // 1-based; first re-prompt is 2
}
```

The re-prompt builder takes a `RePromptContext` and produces a fresh `Sanitized<string>` system+user message pair instructing the model to repair the offending paths. The error list is rendered as a bulleted block with each `path` plus its `message`. No secrets in the re-prompt — by construction (sanitizer was the only entry door).

### 2.3 Repository-Style Interfaces

| Interface | Role | Default impl | Test/alt impls |
|---|---|---|---|
| `LLMClient` | Strategy for all LLM calls. The factory picks one per process. | `AnthropicLLMClient` (when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` available); `OllamaLLMClient` (when configured); `NullLLMClient` (when `LLM_PROVIDER=none`, missing key, or Ollama unreachable on probe) | `RecordingLLMClient` (records prompts/responses for golden tests); `FakeLLMClient` (returns canned responses for hermetic CI) |
| `LLMClientFactory` | Reads `ProviderConfig`, returns the right strategy. | One implementation; no plug points needed. | — |
| `AuditLogWriter` | Consumed from FEAT-006. Every `LLMClient` call writes through it via the wrapper (TASK-010). | Provided by `packages/core/src/audit/` (FEAT-006). | In-memory writer for unit tests. |

The `LLMClient` strategy pattern is the **only** way to swap providers — there is no other extension point, no plugin loader, no DI container. Explicit constructor params per memory.md.

### 2.4 Relationships

| Relationship | Cardinality | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|
| `LLMClient` ↔ provider implementation | 1:1 per process (factory chooses once) | `LLMClientFactory.create()` |
| `LLMClient.generatePlan` call → `agent.jsonl` entries | 1:N (N = 2 × attempts; one `request`+`response` per attempt) | TASK-010 audit wrapper |
| `generatePlan` attempt → `Plan` validated | 1:1 on success | Plan validator (TASK-008) |
| `generatePlan` failure → `RePromptContext` | 1:1 per retry; max `budget.maxCalls` total | TASK-009 bounded re-prompt loop |
| `Sanitized<T>` value → originating `sanitize()` call | 1:1 by construction (brand + runtime registry) | TASK-011 sanitizer-guard |
| `LLMClient.providerId` → audit `provider_id` field | 1:1 every entry | TASK-010 |
| `TOOL_CATALOG` from FEAT-002 → `AgentTool[]` consumed by pi-agent-core | N:N transformation at startup | TASK-002 adapter |

### 2.5 Future DB Schema (Phase 2+)

When persistence moves to SQLite/Postgres alongside the daemon, the JSONL audit log becomes a table. The shape mirrors `AgentJsonlEntry`:

```sql
CREATE TABLE agent_calls (
  call_id              BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  run_id               TEXT NOT NULL,            -- FK -> runs.run_id
  task_id              TEXT NOT NULL,            -- FK -> tasks.task_id
  direction            TEXT NOT NULL,            -- 'request' | 'response'
  provider_id          TEXT NOT NULL,            -- e.g. 'anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-...'
  model                TEXT NOT NULL,
  prompt_sanitized     TEXT NOT NULL,            -- guaranteed-sanitized
  system_prompt_hash   TEXT NOT NULL,            -- sha256
  response_json        JSONB NOT NULL,
  tool_calls_json      JSONB NOT NULL,
  latency_ms           INTEGER NOT NULL,
  cost_usd             NUMERIC(10, 6),           -- null for local providers
  attempt              INTEGER NOT NULL,
  outcome              TEXT NOT NULL,
  ts                   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  INDEX idx_agent_calls_run_ts (run_id, ts)
);
```

Secrets never appear in this table (or its JSONL precursor). The `prompt_sanitized` column is the *output* of FEAT-006's sanitizer; by construction it contains no literal credentials or unredacted PII (within the chosen profile).

## 4. Dependencies

**Internal**:
- **FEAT-001** — Monorepo scaffold, ESLint import-restriction rule (forbids `pi-agent-core` outside this package), `LLM_PROVIDER` CI matrix dimension, Vitest+fast-check baseline.
- **FEAT-002** — `Plan` Zod schema, vendor-neutral `ToolCatalog` emit from `packages/protocol/generated/tool-catalog.ts`, `validateSemantics()` (consumed by `plan/validate.ts`), `ValidationError` shape, `SCHEMA_VERSION` const, `UsageCall` type.
- **FEAT-006** — `sanitize()` chokepoint (the *only* producer of `Sanitized<T>`); `AuditLogWriter` interface and per-run instance (consumed by `audit/wrap.ts`); `KeychainProvider` (consumed by `AnthropicLLMClient` for API-key lookup).

**External (runtime)**:
- **`pi-agent-core`** ([earendil-works/pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/agent/README.md)) — latest stable; **only allowed in this package** (ESLint enforced).
- **`zod`** — peer dep from `@yantra/protocol`; we don't add a separate version.
- **`pino`** — workspace baseline logger.

**External (dev/test)**:
- `vitest`, `fast-check`, `@types/node`, `typescript` — workspace.
- No mocks of `pi-agent-core` are shipped as runtime code; test doubles live under `tests/`.

**Forbidden imports** (lint-enforced):
- Anything from `packages/core/*` — `packages/agent` cannot import `core` (compiler+lint enforced, per memory.md). The sanitizer and audit-log writer are consumed via *types* imported from `@yantra/protocol` (where shared) or via *constructor-injected instances* passed from `apps/cli` — the agent never reaches into `core` directly.
  - **Practical mechanism**: `LLMClient` factory accepts `{ sanitizer, auditLogWriter, keychainProvider }` parameters typed as interfaces defined in `@yantra/protocol` (re-exported from there for cross-package use) or in a new tiny `packages/contracts` if FEAT-006 promotes them. See "Deviations Flagged" — this is the one shape coordination point with FEAT-006 to settle during implementation.
- Any direct `import 'pi-agent-core'` outside `packages/agent/src/client/*` — caught by ESLint + a CI grep (TASK-010 includes the grep script).

## 5. Implementation Tasks

> Each task is a vertical slice. Sizes target half-a-day completion with property tests where mandated. Tasks are ordered for incremental integration: 001–003 give a working AnthropicLLMClient against a canned tool; 004–005 fill out the provider matrix; 006 wires the factory; 007–009 build the plan flow; 010–011 close the audit and sanitizer guarantees; 012 wires FEAT-007's seam; 013–014 deliver the golden + drift suites.

### TASK-001 — `LLMClient` interface + `Sanitized<T>` brand + `LLMError` union

- Author `src/client/interface.ts` with `LLMClient`, `LLMBudget`, `GeneratePlanOpts`, `SummarizeOpts`, `AgentJsonlEntry`.
- Author `src/sanitizer-guard.ts` with `Sanitized<T>`, `brandSanitized<T>()`, `assertSanitized()`. The runtime registry is a `WeakSet` for objects + a bounded LRU `Map<string, true>` for strings (cap 10_000).
- Author `src/errors.ts` deriving custom error classes from `LLMError` variants.
- **Type-level test** (`tests/client/interface.spec.ts`) using TS `expect-error` annotations: `client.generatePlan({ sanitizedPrompt: "raw" })` must fail typecheck; `client.generatePlan({ sanitizedPrompt: brandSanitized("ok") })` must compile. Vitest's typecheck mode (`vitest --typecheck`) runs these.
- **Unit test**: `assertSanitized` throws `SanitizerGuardError` on a raw string; passes on `brandSanitized(...)` output.

**Acceptance**: every `LLMError` variant has a derived `Error` class; `Sanitized<string>` is structurally incompatible with `string` at the call site of `generatePlan` (compile error reproducible).

### TASK-002 — `pi-agent-core` adapter (`pi-adapter.ts`)

- Build a thin adapter that converts FEAT-002's vendor-neutral `ToolCatalog` (emitted from `packages/protocol/generated/tool-catalog.ts` — each entry is `{ name, description, input_schema: JSONSchema, output_schema: JSONSchema | null }`) into pi-agent-core's `AgentTool[]` shape (per the README — `{ name, label, description, parameters (Typebox), executionMode?, execute }`).
- Since the catalog carries JSON Schema (not Typebox), the adapter must round-trip JSON Schema → Typebox. Approach: hand-write a thin walker over our closed Zod-emitted JSON-Schema shape (we control it — it's not arbitrary JSON Schema) into Typebox calls. Bounded scope: `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `null`, `array`, `object`, `enum`, `union`. ~150 LOC, fully tested with one fixture per shape.
- The adapter exposes `toolCatalogToAgentTools(catalog, executeHooks): AgentTool[]`. `executeHooks` is `{ onBeforeToolCall, onAfterToolCall }` — used by the audit wrapper to record every emitted plan step from the agent's perspective; in MVP the `execute` body returns a stub `{ content: [], details: {} }` because **the agent never executes tools — it emits a plan**. We use pi-agent-core's tool-call extraction as the *output channel*, not as ReAct.
- **`pi-adapter.ts` is the ONLY file in the entire monorepo that imports pi-agent-core's tool-definition types**. CI grep enforces this; FEAT-002's import-restriction lint rule already forbids `pi-agent-core` everywhere except `packages/agent/src/client/` and `packages/agent/src/pi-adapter.ts`.
- **Unit test**: round-trip a known `ToolDefinition` (e.g., `FillStep`'s shape) through the adapter; pi-agent-core's Typebox validates a known-good `Step` instance against the resulting `parameters`.
- **Unit test**: every pi-agent-core event (`agent_start`, `agent_end`, `turn_start`, `turn_end`, `message_start`, `message_update`, `message_end`, `tool_execution_*`) is plumbed into a passed-in `EventSink` — verified with a fake sink that asserts presence.

**Acceptance**: an `AgentTool[]` produced from the emitted `TOOL_CATALOG` passes pi-agent-core's own validation when constructed.

### TASK-003 — `AnthropicLLMClient`

- Implement `AnthropicLLMClient` (`src/client/anthropic.ts`) using `pi-agent-core`'s `getModel("anthropic", model)` per README. Constructor accepts `{ apiKey, model, budget, eventSink }`.
- **API key resolution**: per `ProviderConfig.anthropic.apiKey`, either reads `process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (kind: env) or calls FEAT-006's `KeychainProvider.get("yantra", "anthropic.api_key")` (kind: keychain). Never logs the key; never includes it in any error message; on missing key returns `LLMUnavailable{reason:"missing_api_key"}` from `generatePlan` rather than throwing at construction (lazy probe — construction must not block).
- **Strict tool-call schema mode**: per pi-agent-core README, parameters use Typebox; pi-agent-core itself enforces strict schema. We don't add a second layer — we rely on pi-agent-core's validation as the first gate, then our Zod parse as the second (defensive against any pi-agent-core escape).
- **`generatePlan`** (high-level, full flow lives in TASK-008): assembles system prompt, creates `Agent` with `systemPrompt` and `model`, subscribes the audit-event sink, calls `agent.prompt(sanitizedPrompt.value)`, extracts the tool-call output, returns the raw response for downstream validation.
- **`summarize`**: builds an `Agent` with the summary-mode system prompt and no tools; calls `agent.prompt(sanitizedInput + ' ' + sanitizedPrompt)`; returns the final assistant text.
- **`providerId`**: returns `` `anthropic:${model}` ``.
- **Tests** (`tests/client/anthropic.spec.ts`, tagged `@requires-llm`):
  - Smoke: a 1-step "navigate to a public URL" intent produces a schema-valid `Plan` against the live API. CI runs in `LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic` dimension only; gated by `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` secret in CI.
  - Latency budget: a contrived `budget.maxLatencyMs: 1` produces `LLMTimeout`, not a hang.
  - Auth failure: a bogus key produces `LLMUnavailable{reason:"missing_api_key"}` — no key bytes in the error message (regex-asserted).

**Acceptance**: `AnthropicLLMClient.generatePlan(...)` against a canned 1-tool catalog returns a schema-valid `Plan` in a live CI smoke test.

### TASK-004 — `OllamaLLMClient`

- Implement `OllamaLLMClient` (`src/client/ollama.ts`) using `pi-agent-core`'s Ollama provider (per pi-agent-core's `getModel(...)` shape; if pi-agent-core exposes Ollama under a different identifier, the adapter inspects the version at construction time and falls back to a direct `fetch` against `${baseUrl}/api/chat` with the equivalent message envelope — documented in code with a TODO comment if the fallback is taken).
- **Base URL**: configurable; default `http://localhost:11434`. Connectivity probe at first `generatePlan` (lazy): on connection refused, returns `LLMUnavailable{reason:"ollama_unreachable"}` with a hint string pointing at `yantra doctor`.
- **Model recommendations** (documented in JSDoc on the constructor and in `prompts/guidance.md`'s "operator notes" appendix — *not* in the prompt itself):
  - `llama3.1:8b` (recommended baseline — broad tool-call support)
  - `qwen2.5:7b` (alternative — good JSON-mode behavior)
  - `mistral-nemo:12b` (when RAM permits — better long-prompt fidelity)
  - Models without tool-call support fall through to JSON-mode (system prompt instructs the model to emit a JSON object matching the `Plan` JSON Schema). If JSON-mode parse fails, `LLMValidationFailed{kind:"llm_validation_failed"}` — same path as a malformed Anthropic response.
- **`providerId`**: returns `` `ollama:${model}@${baseUrlHost}` ``.
- **Tests**:
  - `@requires-llm` smoke (gated by `OLLAMA_CI=1`): same canned intent as TASK-003; assert schema-valid Plan.
  - `@no-llm` connectivity-failure test: an `OllamaLLMClient` pointed at an unreachable URL returns `LLMUnavailable{reason:"ollama_unreachable"}` from `generatePlan`.

**Acceptance**: when both `OLLAMA_CI=1` and `ANTHROPIC_CI=1` are set, the provider-drift suite (TASK-014) can construct both clients and submit the same prompt.

### TASK-005 — `NullLLMClient`

- Implement `NullLLMClient` (`src/client/null.ts`): every method (`generatePlan`, `summarize`) returns `Result.err({ kind: "llm_unavailable", reason: "provider_none", hint: "Configure LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic or =ollama; see `yantra doctor`." })` immediately. No I/O, no allocation beyond the error object.
- `providerId`: returns `"null"`.
- The audit wrapper still wraps `NullLLMClient` — its calls produce `agent.jsonl` entries with `outcome: "provider_error"` and `prompt_sanitized` populated. This preserves the audit-trail-first invariant even in `--no-llm` runs (a caller's intent to call the LLM is recorded; the absence of a response is recorded too).
- **Tests** (`@no-llm`): every method returns `LLMUnavailable`; the `agent.jsonl` audit row is emitted; no `pi-agent-core` import is reachable in this module (verified by a static check on the bundled output).

**Acceptance**: full `apps/cli` `ask --no-llm` test passes; the rule-based path in FEAT-007 takes over without an unhandled exception.

### TASK-006 — `LLMClient` factory

- Author `src/client/factory.ts` with `createLLMClient(config, deps)` returning the right strategy.
- **Resolution rules**:
  1. If `LLM_PROVIDER=none` (env or config) → `NullLLMClient`.
  2. If `provider: "anthropic"`: check API key per `ProviderConfig.anthropic.apiKey`; if missing, `pino.warn("anthropic configured but no API key found; degrading to none")` and return `NullLLMClient`. If present, return `AnthropicLLMClient`.
  3. If `provider: "ollama"`: construct `OllamaLLMClient` eagerly; defer connectivity check to first call (lazy probe).
  4. If `provider: "openai"`: log `pino.warn("openai not supported in MVP")` and return `NullLLMClient`. Phase 2 leaves a clear seam.
  5. Otherwise (`unknown` value): log a warning + return `NullLLMClient`.
- Always returns *something* — never throws. Per memory.md §Error Handling: no silent failure, but also no fatal-at-startup.
- **Tests** (`@no-llm`): every branch, including the "anthropic configured but no key" warning (assert the log fires; assert no key bytes appear in the log message).

**Acceptance**: `yantra doctor` (FEAT-003 + FEAT-012) calls the factory and reports `providerId` correctly across all five cases.

### TASK-007 — System-prompt assembly (`prompts/assemble.ts` + `guidance.md`)

- Author `assemble(opts: AssembleOpts): SystemPromptAssembly` — a pure function. No I/O at runtime; `guidanceMarkdown` is injected by the caller (factory reads `guidance.md` once at startup).
- **Assembled structure** (top-down):
  1. **Header**: `"You are Yantra's plan generator. Schema version: 0.1. Emit a Plan that conforms exactly to the tool-call schema below."`
  2. **Hand-written guidance** (from `guidance.md`): role definition (browser-automation orchestrator, narrow tool catalog), core principles, **"NEVER invent CSS/XPath/role selectors — always reference locators by workflow name or structured intent"**, scope rules (read-only-data restricts to non-mutating verbs), security guarantees the user expects, output discipline (one tool call per Step, no prose).
  3. **Generated tool catalog**: enumerated from `toolDefs` — name, one-line description (from FEAT-002's `.describe()`), abbreviated input shape. Long-form schemas are not embedded; pi-agent-core delivers the full Typebox to the model itself.
  4. **Schema-version footer**: `"Emit schema_version: \"0.1\". Plans must contain 1–64 steps. Step IDs are s1, s2, s3, ..."`
- **Determinism contract**: `assemble(x) === assemble(x)` byte-for-byte. Property-tested with arbitrary tool-def permutations: the function sorts tool defs by name (stable canonical order) before rendering so input-order changes do not perturb the output.
- **`guidance.md` content rules**: kept under 2KB; ASCII-only (token-stable across model tokenizers); reviewed like code (no autogeneration). Includes a "do/don't" examples block.
- **Tests**: determinism property test (1000 runs); known-good snapshot of `text` against a small fixture toolset; `fullHash` matches independent SHA-256 computation.

**Acceptance**: the assembled prompt's `fullHash` is stable across consecutive `pnpm test` runs and across all three CI OSes.

### TASK-008 — `generatePlan` orchestration (`plan/generate.ts`)

- The end-to-end flow inside any concrete `LLMClient.generatePlan`:
  1. **Sanitizer check** (cheap, defense-in-depth — `Sanitized<>` already enforced at the type level): `assertSanitized(opts.sanitizedPrompt)`.
  2. **System-prompt assembly** via TASK-007.
  3. **Call**: `client.rawCall(systemPrompt, opts.sanitizedPrompt.value, agentTools)` — provider-specific; returns the raw response.
  4. **Schema validation**: `opts.schema.safeParse(extractedToolCall)` → if `success: false`, build `RePromptContext` and retry (TASK-009).
  5. **Semantic validation**: `validateSemantics(plan, opts.workflowContext)` → if errors, same retry path.
  6. On success: `Result.ok(plan)`.
- The orchestration is implemented once in `plan/generate.ts` and called by both `AnthropicLLMClient.generatePlan` and `OllamaLLMClient.generatePlan`. The provider-specific code is the **`rawCall`** internal method (not on the interface — interface remains `generatePlan` only).
- **Tests** (`@no-llm`, with `FakeLLMClient` returning canned responses):
  - Happy path: 1 call → schema-valid → semantic-valid → `Result.ok(plan)`.
  - Schema-fail-then-succeed: first call returns malformed JSON; re-prompt; second call returns valid → `Result.ok(plan)` with `attempt: 2` in audit log.
  - Max-retries-exhausted: every call returns malformed → `Result.err({ kind: "llm_validation_failed", attempts: 3, errors: [...] })`.
  - Budget-exhausted: `budget.maxCalls: 1`; one failure → `Result.err({ kind: "llm_budget_exhausted" })` (not retried).
  - Semantic failure with workflow context: `CaptureRef` to non-existent step → returns `llm_validation_failed` with the precise JSON-pointer path from FEAT-002's validator.

**Acceptance**: a fixture intent + canned malformed-then-valid responses produce a single `Result.ok(plan)` in 2 attempts, with both audit-log entries written.

### TASK-009 — Bounded re-prompt (`prompts/reprompt.ts`)

- Implement `buildRePrompt(ctx: RePromptContext, opts: AssembleOpts): { systemPrompt: SystemPromptAssembly; userMessage: Sanitized<string> }`.
- The re-prompt user message is a structured block:
  ```
  Your previous plan failed validation. Repair the issues below and emit a complete corrected Plan.

  Issues:
    - /steps/3/locator/name: locator name "Sign in!" not found in workflow's _locators block
    - /steps/5: step in read-only-data scope cannot be a click step
    - /outputs/0/from: capture_as "transactions" is not produced by any prior ExtractStep
  ```
- The `userMessage` is **already sanitized by construction** — it contains only protocol JSON-pointer paths and error codes (`ValidationError.code`), no user-supplied content, no captured DOM. It is branded via the same `brandSanitized` path (registered as exempt — see Deviations §1) because the inputs are fully under our control.
- **Default `budget.maxCalls = 3`** (1 initial + 2 retries, matching memory.md §Error Handling "max 2 retries").
- Each retry counts against `budget.maxCalls`. Final failure returns `LLMValidationFailed{attempts, errors}` aggregating the *last* attempt's errors only (avoids confusing union-of-all-errors output).
- **Tests** (`@no-llm`): structural format snapshot; idempotence (same `ctx` → same output); no secrets ever appear (property test: feed an arbitrary `ValidationError[]` with synthetic credential-shaped `.message` text; assert the renderer does not include any `sk-`/`ghp_`/`AKIA`/`eyJ` substring — defense in depth).

**Acceptance**: a malformed plan whose JSON-pointer paths point at three distinct fields produces a re-prompt that pi-agent-core successfully completes against on attempt 2 in the golden suite (TASK-013).

### TASK-010 — Audit wrapper + UsageWriter integration + CI guard (`audit/wrap.ts` + scripts)

- Implement `wrapWithAudit(client: LLMClient, writer: AuditLogWriter, usageWriter: UsageWriter, runId: string): LLMClient` — a higher-order that returns an `LLMClient` whose every method (a) emits an `AgentJsonlEntry` with `direction: "request"` before the underlying call, (b) emits one with `direction: "response"` after (including on error — `outcome: "timeout" | "provider_error" | "validation_failed"`), (c) **writes a `UsageCall` to `usageWriter` (FEAT-005) on every successful response** with the same `step_id`/`run_id`/`task_id` correlation, (d) propagates the underlying result unchanged.
- **Token counts**: extracted from pi-agent-core's response event payload (`input_tokens`, `output_tokens`). Stored in both `AgentJsonlEntry` and the `UsageCall` row.
- **`cost_estimate_usd` calculation**: model-id → per-token-cost lookup table (`src/client/pricing.ts`, small static map). `null` for Ollama (local). The table is **not** authoritative — it's a best-effort cost estimate; the `yantra audit` and `yantra usage` views label it as an estimate in human output.
- **Latency**: `performance.now()` before/after; `latency_ms` rounded to integer.
- **`generatePlan` aggregation across re-prompts**: the wrapper emits one `UsageCall` *per underlying provider call* (request/response pair) so re-prompts show as separate rows. The `GeneratePlanResult.usage` returned to the caller is the **sum** of all those rows (input_tokens, output_tokens, cost) — the caller sees the bottom line; the audit shows the per-attempt detail.
- **Wrapper enforcement**:
  - **Runtime**: the factory (TASK-006) *always* wraps its return value with `wrapWithAudit`. An unwrapped `LLMClient` is never exposed outside this package — the factory's return type is `LLMClient` (interface), so consumers cannot tell the difference, but `apps/cli` never sees a bare provider.
  - **Static**: `scripts/verify-llm-call-wrapping.ts` — greps `packages/*/src` and `apps/*/src` for any direct `pi-agent-core` import outside `packages/agent/src/client/`; greps for any construction of `AnthropicLLMClient`/`OllamaLLMClient`/`NullLLMClient` outside `packages/agent/src/client/factory.ts`. CI runs this on every PR.
- **Tests**: a fake `AuditLogWriter` and fake `UsageWriter` (both in-memory) verify that every `generatePlan` and `summarize` call (success and failure) produces exactly 2 `AgentJsonlEntry`s (request + response) and (on success) exactly 1 `UsageCall` per underlying provider call; assertion that the `prompt_sanitized` field equals the input's unwrapped string (no double-sanitization, no missing-sanitization); assertion that `GeneratePlanResult.usage.input_tokens` equals the sum of per-attempt `UsageCall.input_tokens`.

**Acceptance**: the CI guard fails the build on a deliberately-introduced rogue `import "pi-agent-core"` in `apps/cli/src/`; the audit-log fake records two entries per `generatePlan`; the usage-writer fake records N rows for an N-attempt re-prompt loop; the returned `GeneratePlanResult.usage` totals match.

### TASK-011 — Sanitizer-guard runtime registry (`sanitizer-guard.ts` part 2)

- Complete `assertSanitized` to consult a process-wide bounded LRU `Map<string, true>` for primitive strings and a `WeakSet<object>` for object inputs.
- FEAT-006's `sanitize()` is updated (or via a small `register()` helper exported from this file) to register every returned `SanitizedPayload.text` (and any nested `Sanitized<>` it produces) in the LRU/WeakSet at the moment of sanitization.
- The LRU is bounded at 10_000 entries (cap on memory growth) with most-recent-first eviction. **Eviction does not invalidate downstream calls**: if a `Sanitized<>` is evicted and a later call passes the same string, `assertSanitized` will refuse it. This is the desired strictness — callers must keep `Sanitized<>` values in scope until they pass them; serialization across process boundaries (Phase 2 daemon) will need a different mechanism, tracked in `TODO.md`.
- **Tests** (`@no-llm`):
  - Property test: any string passed through FEAT-006's `sanitize()` then `assertSanitized` does not throw; any arbitrary string (not previously sanitized) throws `SanitizerGuardError`.
  - Property test: every `LLMClient` method, given a raw string cast to `Sanitized<string>` via `as` (bypassing the type system), throws at runtime — verifying the belt-and-suspenders contract.

**Acceptance**: `Sanitized<>` is unforgeable in practice — the only successful paths are through `sanitize()` or through the explicit re-prompt builder's controlled brand call (registered in the same registry).

On `Result.ok(text)`, the result becomes the card body; on `Result.err({kind:"llm_unavailable"})`, FEAT-007 falls through to its first-N-sentence rule-based summary (works under `--no-llm`).

### TASK-013 — Golden-plan suite plumbing (`e2e/golden/`)

- Author the golden-fixture format in `e2e/golden/README.md`:
  - One `.golden.json` per canonical intent. Shape: `{ intent: string, provider_id: string, model: string, schema_version: "0.1", plan: Plan }`.
  - Filename: `<slug>.<provider_id>.golden.json` (the `provider_id` segment lets us pin per-model, regenerated on bump).
- Author a `RecordingLLMClient` (`src/client/recording.ts`): wraps any `LLMClient`; on success, writes the produced `Plan` to `e2e/golden/<slug>.<providerId>.golden.json` (created if absent, diff-checked if present). On diff, fails the test with a side-by-side report.
- Author the comparator: a small `e2e/golden/run.spec.ts` that loads each `.golden.json`, submits the `intent` to the configured `LLMClient`, and asserts equality (deep-equal modulo non-determinism: `task_id` and `plan_id` are stripped before comparison — ULIDs change per run).
- **Populating canonical plans is MVP dogfooding** — not in this feature's scope. Plumbing is. The directory ships with a `.gitkeep` and `README.md`.
- CI runs the suite on every dependency bump of `pi-agent-core` *or* every model-id change in `config.yaml` (a Turborepo `inputs` declaration triggers re-run). Intentional changes go through `pnpm --filter @yantra/agent golden:rerecord` + reviewer confirmation.

**Acceptance**: the suite skeleton runs green with zero `.golden.json` files (no-op pass); adding a malformed `.golden.json` produces an actionable failure.

### TASK-014 — Provider-drift test (`tests-integration/provider-drift.spec.ts`)

- A nightly-only suite (CI cron, not PR-blocking) tagged `@requires-llm`.
- Setup: construct both `AnthropicLLMClient` and `OllamaLLMClient` from the same `ToolDef[]` and the same assembled system prompt.
- For each of N canonical intents (small set, e.g. 5 — same intents as the golden suite):
  - Submit `intent` to both clients.
  - Assert each `Result.ok(plan)`.
  - Assert each `plan` passes schema validation (the *same* schema validation as production).
  - **Do not** assert plan-equivalence between providers — that's expected to drift in shape. Schema validity is the universal contract; semantic equivalence is a Phase 2 question.
- Output: a small markdown report (`agent-drift-<date>.md`) summarising which providers' plans diverged in step count, in scope assignment, in extraction shape — useful for guidance.md tuning.
- **Skip gate**: skips cleanly if either `ANTHROPIC_CI=1` or `OLLAMA_CI=1` is not set; emits a `pino.info` so the CI run is auditable.

**Acceptance**: nightly CI on a fresh machine produces a drift report green; deliberately breaking one provider's schema conformance fails the suite with a clear diff.

## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

### Auth

- **API keys live in the OS keychain**, not in `config.yaml`. Keys: `anthropic.api_key` (under service `yantra`). FEAT-006's `KeychainProvider` is the only path. Env-var fallback (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) is honored for CI ergonomics; documented in `yantra doctor`'s output as a "keychain preferred" hint.
- **Keys are never logged.** Pino's secret-shape redactor (FEAT-006) is the safety net; the primary guarantee is reviewer + this file's TASK-003 test that asserts no key bytes appear in error messages.
- **Ollama needs no auth** for default local installs; if `OLLAMA_HOST` requires auth, it is configured per pi-agent-core's mechanism (Phase 2 — MVP assumes local).
- **No key in audit log.** `AgentJsonlEntry.provider_id` includes the provider name and model, never the key.

### Error Handling

- Every public method returns `Result<T, LLMError>`. No method throws across a package boundary in success/expected-failure flows. Unexpected programmer errors (e.g., `assertSanitized` failure, invalid `ProviderConfig` shape after the factory's defensive parse) throw `Error`-derived classes — distinct from `LLMError` and unrecoverable by design.
- **`LLMUnavailable` is typed, not silent.** Consumers pattern-match. FEAT-007's `ask` pipeline falls through to rule-based on `kind:"llm_unavailable"`. FEAT-012's CLI renders a one-line actionable message ("LLM not configured — run `yantra doctor` to set it up, or pass `--no-llm` to force the rule-based path").
- **Bounded re-prompt is server-side authoritative.** Callers cannot raise the retry budget by retrying themselves — every retry counts against `budget.maxCalls`. The `LLMError.kind:"llm_budget_exhausted"` outcome is the explicit signal.
- **No `process.exit` anywhere in this package.** Memory.md §Error Handling.

### Logging

- Every `LLMClient` call → **2 `agent.jsonl` entries** (request + response), per memory.md §Logging mandatory audit events.
- Every plan generation emits a `pino.info` with `{provider_id, model, attempts, latency_ms, cost_estimate_usd}` — no prompt or response content (the JSONL is the canonical record).
- Every re-prompt emits `pino.warn({attempt, errors_count, first_error_path})` — operators can scan for prompt-engineering regressions.
- Every `kind: "llm_validation_failed"` final outcome emits `pino.error({attempts, errors})`; the run aborts and a `task_failed` event is emitted with `failure_class: "validation_error"` (per FEAT-002's `FailureClass` enum) — wired in FEAT-005's executor, surfaced from here as the structured `LLMError`.
- **No `console.log`** anywhere. Pino only. Memory.md §Logging.

### Security

- **`Sanitized<>` brand is the single most important pattern in this feature.** The compile-time half is non-negotiable (TS strict + no `any` in this package, per memory.md). The runtime registry is defense in depth. The CI grep on direct `pi-agent-core` imports closes the third hole.
- **CI static-analysis guards** delivered in this feature:
  1. `scripts/verify-no-pi-agent-core-imports.ts` — fails the build on any `import 'pi-agent-core'` outside `packages/agent/src/client/`.
  2. `scripts/verify-llm-call-wrapping.ts` — fails the build on any direct construction of provider clients outside `factory.ts`.
  3. (Coordinated with FEAT-006) — the existing sanitizer-call-required check from FEAT-006 covers every `LLMClient.send` call site; this feature adds **call-site coverage tests** that exercise the grep against deliberate violations in a fixture.
- **`pino` redactor configured** (per FEAT-006) — defense in depth on the off-chance a secret-shaped string slips into a log statement.
- **No literal credentials in tests.** Synthetic shapes only: `fake-sk-FOOBAR`, `ghp_TESTDATA…`, etc. Same convention as FEAT-002.
- **CI matrix mandates both `LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic` and `LLM_PROVIDER=none`** — memory.md §Testing. Tests tagged `@no-llm` (the majority — `NullLLMClient`, sanitizer-guard, factory branches, generate flow with `FakeLLMClient`, audit wrapper, assemble determinism) pass in both. Tests tagged `@requires-llm` skip cleanly in `none`.

### Testing

- **`@no-llm` is the default**. Only TASK-003, TASK-004 live-provider smoke, and TASK-014 drift test are `@requires-llm`.
- **`pi-agent-core` is mocked where appropriate** for hermetic CI: a `FakePiAgentCore` lives under `tests/` (not `src/` — never shipped) that emits a configurable scripted sequence of events. Used by TASK-008's flow tests and TASK-010's audit-wrapper tests.
- **Property-based tests (mandatory)**:
  1. `assemble` determinism (TASK-007).
  2. `assertSanitized` correctness (TASK-011) — every sanitized string passes, every non-sanitized string fails.
  3. Re-prompt renderer (TASK-009) — never includes a credential-shaped substring across arbitrary error inputs.
- **AAA pattern** (per memory.md).
- **Factories**: `makeSanitized()`, `makeToolDefs()`, `makePlan()`, `makeRePromptContext()` — shared under `tests/factories.ts`.
- **Coverage target**: 95%+ on `plan/generate.ts`, `audit/wrap.ts`, `sanitizer-guard.ts`, `client/factory.ts` (the trust-boundary surfaces). Don't chase coverage on adapter glue.

### Dogfooding Acceptance Test (manual, before marking complete)

The author of the implementation must verify, before flipping the status:

1. `pnpm --filter @yantra/agent build` succeeds clean on macOS, Windows, and Ubuntu.
2. `pnpm --filter @yantra/agent test` passes 100% in both `LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic` (with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set) and `LLM_PROVIDER=none` CI dimensions.
3. With `LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic`, `yantra ask "what time is it in Tokyo right now?"` produces a card whose summary text was clearly LLM-generated (the synthesis path lit up via TASK-012), with `agent.jsonl` containing exactly 2 entries (request + response), `provider_id: anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-...`, `cost_estimate_usd > 0`, and `prompt_sanitized` containing no PII patterns from the query.
4. With `LLM_PROVIDER=none`, the same `yantra ask` command returns a rule-based summary (FEAT-007's fallback) with `agent.jsonl` containing exactly 2 entries showing `outcome: "provider_error"` and `provider_id: "null"` — the audit trail records the *intent* to call even when no LLM is available.
5. Hand-construct a deliberately-malformed prompt expectation (intent that the agent is likely to misjudge — e.g., "give me a plan that fills my password into a Google search box"); verify the agent emits a `Plan` that either (a) refuses (no `FillStep` against `password`) or (b) emits a malformed plan that the semantic validator catches; in case (b), confirm exactly 2 re-prompt attempts before final `kind: "llm_validation_failed"` with structured errors and no run aborting outside the typed-error path.
6. Run `tests-integration/provider-drift.spec.ts` once locally with both `ANTHROPIC_CI=1` and `OLLAMA_CI=1`; confirm both providers produce schema-valid plans on all canonical intents.

## Deviations Flagged

- **Re-prompt user message is itself branded `Sanitized<>` via a controlled call to `brandSanitized` inside `prompts/reprompt.ts`.** The reasoning: the re-prompt body contains only protocol JSON-pointer paths and `ValidationError.code` strings — inputs fully under our control, never user-supplied. A property test (TASK-009) asserts no credential shape can appear in the rendered output. This is the one place outside FEAT-006's `sanitize()` where `brandSanitized` is permitted; the ESLint import-pattern allowlist must include `packages/agent/src/prompts/reprompt.ts`. Calling out because it weakens the "sanitize() is the only producer" rule in exchange for keeping the type system uniform. Alternative considered: a second branded type `InternallySafe<>` — rejected as fragmentation that obscures the simpler one-brand-one-meaning model.

- **Interface shapes for `Sanitizer`, `AuditLogWriter`, and `KeychainProvider` need a cross-package home** since `packages/agent` cannot import `packages/core` (per memory.md). Two options: (a) re-export these types from `packages/protocol` (where contract types already live); (b) introduce a tiny `packages/contracts` that both `core` and `agent` depend on. Recommendation: **option (a)** — `protocol` already owns `ValidationError`, `Plan`, etc.; adding three interface types keeps the dep graph flat. To be confirmed during FEAT-006 implementation; if FEAT-006 already chose otherwise, this spec adopts that choice. Flagging for the plan-critic.

- **`LLMSummarizeStep` is a Plan step (FEAT-002, executor in FEAT-005), and `LLMClient.summarize` is a CLI-layer call from `ask` (FEAT-007).** These are different code paths — the former is reached by the executor walking a `Plan`; the latter is reached directly by `ask` before any Plan exists. Both flow through the same audit wrapper and sanitizer guard; both are tracked in `agent.jsonl`. Calling out to prevent confusion: this feature owns the `LLMClient.summarize` invocation; the `LLMSummarizeStep` execution path is FEAT-005's responsibility (which itself uses `LLMClient.summarize` under the hood — single chokepoint).

- **`generatePlan` lights up the `ask` LLM synthesis path in MVP, not a full `do` task.** The plan.md feature one-liner mentions `do` in Phase 2. The `LLMClient.generatePlan` surface is built fully here (tested with `FakeLLMClient` end-to-end including re-prompt), so when `do` lands in Phase 2 it is a wiring change, not a re-implementation. MVP's first real consumer of `generatePlan` is **the test suite + golden harness** — production `ask` uses `summarize` only. Calling out because the user's one-liner could be read as "generatePlan ships unused in MVP"; that is technically true, but the surface ships fully validated.

- **Default re-prompt budget is `maxCalls: 3` (1 initial + 2 retries)**, matching memory.md §Error Handling's "max 2 retries" wording. The `budget` field on `LLMBudget` is `maxCalls`, not `maxRetries`, to avoid the off-by-one confusion that plagues re-prompt code; documented inline.

- **`pi-agent-core` Ollama provider availability is unverified at spec time.** The README excerpt available to this spec confirms Anthropic and OpenAI provider identifiers but does not confirm Ollama's. TASK-004 includes a runtime-introspection fallback (direct `fetch` against `/api/chat`) if the package does not expose Ollama. Flagging as a known unknown; resolved at implementation time. If pi-agent-core has no Ollama path even at implementation, the fallback becomes the primary implementation.

- **Cost estimates are best-effort.** The static `pricing.ts` table will drift behind provider price changes. Surfaced as `cost_estimate_usd` in human audit output; treated as advisory in the data model. A `null` value is always acceptable; consumers must handle it.

- **Token-streaming output (`pi-agent-core`'s `message_update`) is recorded in `agent.jsonl` (request/response entries capture the final response only) but is not surfaced to the CLI in MVP.** FEAT-012 may opt into streaming under `--debug`. Documented in TODO.md.
